experiments.scope: The exact sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1 target. Once per run it checks the 6-round hash against two known-answer digests of the organizer reference and the 24-round version against hashlib.sha3_256, rank 40 of W40 and the 780 basis-pair two-round polarizations of Lemma 3 (a failed check stops it). Trials 256g..256g+255 form one group: group index h = int(seed of the group's first trial, 16) mod G and trial k is lane c = k mod 256 of the cosets j = 256h + c. The leader step draws each coset origin t_j from two random words taken from the trial's own coins; here they are the two halves of SHAKE-256 of the trial's seed, a reproducible stand-in, not the attack's randomness source. The trials of a group share one table, so they are not independent repetitions. The group executes the reference schedule of proof.md Sections 5.3, 5.4, 6 and 7 (shared with the claimed route, introduction of Section 5) at reduced size: the first 2^9 Gray points of each coset with degree bound 8, all 175 planes, the full 140-bit key, the constant-folded bit-sliced setup of all 256 cosets at every point (bitplanes, generated code of rounds 0 to 5), the transpose of every record into candidate-major words, the candidate-major FES of each lane with the key formed in the word (no key transpose), the value-masked table with 2^17 candidates whose never-written words start with fixed pseudo-random content, and native verification of key matches. Every operation runs through a counting machine and the program stops unless each executed count equals the formula of proof.md. It then executes the claimed route's setup code (eight XOR-forms of the planes, dead operations removed: 32 points, transform, phase) and its plane-major FES with the filter word on all 512 Gray points, counted, and stops unless the filter word equals the survivors of the emitted keys (proof.md Sections 5.5, 6.3). Beside the algorithm, one candidate per Gray point is hashed natively and its key compared with the emitted key.
experiments.hypothesis: No trial returns a pair: a 256-bit collision among 2^17 messages has probability below 2^-222. The run shows that the shipped program executes the schedule end to end on the target with the declared operation counts. Its 16 untrusted numbers satisfy: own_pairs16 (per trial) = the number of unordered pairs of the trial's 512 candidates whose keys agree on 16 digest bits (uniform digests give 1.996 per trial and 511 per 256 trials); the other 15 are the same for every trial of a group: fes_ops = 845059 (256 x 3301 + 3); buffer_reads = 261632 (here the frame copies, 2 per record word: 256 x 2 x 511); chi_transpose_ops = 4772232 (here the key, 6 per candidate, and the record transposes, 7800 per record: 786432 + 3985800); table_ops = 6 (131072 - x - m) + 14 x + 10 m with x = in_range_mismatches (false tag passes) and m = key_matches; sparse_inserts = 131072 - m; leader_ops = 2821 (11 per coset and 5 per group); setup_group_ops = 13616 (the transpose); setup_point_ops = 31720302 (62022 per point at 511 points plus twice the popcount sum 13530); transform_phase_ops = 2419200; verify_check_ops at most 2438 (a valid hit, 10, and one verification, at most 2428); perm_calls = 0 (verification evaluates the six rounds in word operations); native_checks = 512; key_mismatch = 0. once_ops = 7666 is asserted inside the program, not reported. Nothing about cost is inferred from the run; own_pairs16 is a 16-bit check of premise H_coset on the trials' own digests, not evidence at 256 bits.

experiments.scope: The same program, target, once-per-run checks, group construction and reduced schedule as experiment fes-campaign-reduced (the reference schedule of proof.md Sections 5.3, 5.4, 6, 7 and 13: one group of 256 cosets whose origins come from the trials' own coins, the first 2^9 Gray points of each coset, all 175 planes, the full 140-bit key, the value-masked table and native verification, through a counting machine that stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md), on the organizer seeds of this experiment, hence an independent group of 256 random-origin cosets. Premise test (proof.md Section 12.2), beside the algorithm: trial k (lane c) returns the first two of the 512 Gray points of its own coset, in Gray order, whose digests agree on the 16 masked bits (bits 0..3 of digest lanes 0..3), found from the emitted keys and checked natively. Different trials use disjoint message sets. The program also executes the claimed route's setup code, plane-major FES and filter word as in fes-campaign-reduced.
experiments.hypothesis: Reduced-width form of premise H_coset on the trials' own random-origin digests. If digests of distinct messages behave as independent uniform values on these 16 bits, a set of 512 contains an agreeing pair with probability P = 1 - prod_{i<512} (1 - i/2^16) = 0.864841510863844, so the organizer-recomputed successes of the 256 trials follow Binomial(256, P): expectation 221.40, standard deviation 5.47, pass interval [200, 243] (expectation +- 4 sd). A mask success is a 16-bit partial match, not a collision. The program also stops unless the group's exact pair counts lie in their pass intervals (expectation +- 4 sd; Var = n p (1 - p), pair indicators of uniform values being pairwise independent): pairs16_within, two points of one coset agreeing on key bits 0..15 (n = 33,488,896 pairs, expectation 511), in [421, 601]; pairs16_cross, points of two different cosets agreeing on bits 0..15 (n = 8,556,380,160, expectation 130,560), in [129115, 132005]; pairs24_cross, the same on bits 0..23 (expectation 510), in [420, 600]. The other 13 observations are the group counts of experiment fes-campaign-reduced except buffer_reads and sparse_inserts, which the program checks without reporting them. Scope: 2^17 digests of one group, 16- and 24-bit projections, 9-dimensional sub-cosets; nothing about 256-bit rates or cost is inferred from the run.

experiments.scope: The same program, target, once-per-run checks, group construction and reduced schedule as experiment fes-campaign-reduced (the reference schedule of proof.md Sections 5.3, 5.4, 6, 7 and 13: one group of 256 cosets whose origins come from the trials' own coins, the first 2^9 Gray points of each coset, all 175 planes, the full 140-bit key, the value-masked table and native verification, through a counting machine that stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md), on the organizer seeds of this experiment, hence an independent group of 256 random-origin cosets. Premise test (proof.md Section 12.2): trial k returns the first Gray point b >= 256 of the partner coset (lane c XOR 1, an independent origin) whose digest agrees on the 16 masked bits (bits 0..3 of digest lanes 0..3) with a Gray point a < 256 of its own coset, and that a, found from the emitted keys and checked natively. Different trials use disjoint message sets: points 0..255 of their own coset and points 256..511 of the partner coset. The program also executes the claimed route's setup code, plane-major FES and filter word as in fes-campaign-reduced.
experiments.hypothesis: Reduced-width form of premise H_coset across cosets with independent uniform origins. If digests of distinct messages behave as independent uniform values on these 16 bits, two disjoint sets of 256 contain an agreeing cross pair with probability P = 0.632121969489614 (exact, from the occupancy law of one set), so the organizer-recomputed successes of the 256 trials follow Binomial(256, P): expectation 161.82, standard deviation 7.72, pass interval [131, 192] (expectation +- 4 sd). A mask success is a 16-bit partial match, not a collision. The program also stops unless the group's exact pair counts lie in the pass intervals stated for experiment hcoset-within16: pairs16_within in [421, 601], pairs16_cross in [129115, 132005], pairs24_cross in [420, 600]; the other 13 observations are as there. Scope: 2^17 digests of one group, 16- and 24-bit projections, 9-dimensional sub-cosets; nothing about 256-bit rates or cost is inferred from the run.

experiments.scope: The same program, target, once-per-run checks, group construction and reduced schedule as experiment hcoset-within16 (the reference schedule of proof.md Sections 5.3, 5.4, 6, 7 and 13: one group of 256 cosets whose origins come from the trials' own coins, the first 2^9 Gray points of each coset, all 175 planes, the full 140-bit key, the value-masked table and native verification, through a counting machine that stops unless every executed count equals the formula of proof.md), on the organizer seeds of this experiment, hence an independent group of 256 random-origin cosets. Survivor test (proof.md Sections 5.5 and 12.2), beside the algorithm: the survivors of the eight-bit filter of the filtered route are the points of the group whose digest bits 0 and 1 of lanes 0..3 are all zero, found from the emitted keys (the key bit of lane 0, bit 0, is the digest bit XOR 1); trial t returns the t-th pair of survivors, in order of the value of their digest bits 2 and 3 of lanes 0..3 and then of the index, that agree on those eight bits, so that the two digests agree on the 16 masked bits; each returned pair is checked natively, with its eight filter bits. The program also executes the claimed route's setup code, plane-major FES and filter word as in fes-campaign-reduced.
experiments.hypothesis: Survivor form of premise H_coset on the trials' own random-origin digests. If digests of distinct messages behave as independent uniform values on the eight filter bits, the number n of survivors among the 2^17 points of the group is Binomial(2^17, 2^-8) (expectation 512, standard deviation 22.6) and the program stops unless 422 <= n <= 602. For uniform values the pairs of survivors that agree on the next eight digest bits (bits 2 and 3 of lanes 0..3) number C(n, 2)/256 in expectation with the variance of a sum of pairwise independent indicators (at most the expectation) and the program stops unless their count lies within 4 standard deviations of it; the interval guarantees at least 273 such pairs, so all 256 trials return one, and the organizer recomputes that both digests agree on the 16 masked bits (bits 0..3 of digest lanes 0..3). The program also stops unless the group pair counts pairs16_within, pairs16_cross and pairs24_cross lie in the intervals of experiment hcoset-within16. A mask success is a 16-bit partial match of two survivors, not a collision. The reported observations are the 13 group counts of fes-campaign-reduced except buffer_reads and sparse_inserts (checked, not reported), survivors8 (the number n) and pairs8_survivors (the pair count). Scope: 2^17 digests of one group, about 512 survivors, 8 further bits, 9-dimensional sub-cosets; nothing about 256-bit rates or cost is inferred from the run.
